clue.text: Mild as can be — so depressing

indicators.note: 'as can be' suggests the letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something as gentle as possible turns out to be thoroughly gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is the anagram signal: MILD AS rearranged gives the answer; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dismal is gloomy and dreary, so it lowers the spirits.

clue.text: In a small garden seedlings should be close-planted

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: seedlings in a small plot should be planted tightly together.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'garDEN SEedlings'; 'a small' is part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants set close together form a thick, crowded mass, which is what dense describes.

clue.text: Needing props, he's the buyer

indicators.note: something needing props is unsteady and falls about, so the letters that follow are knocked into a new order

parts.note: 'he's' gives he, with the 's standing for 'is' as a link

explanation.surface: A man who needs support is the one doing the purchasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing' signals the anagram of PROPS HE: a thing needing props would topple over.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper is a person out purchasing goods, a customer or buyer.

clue.text: The person planning for a constructive follow-up

definitions.text: The person planning for a constructive follow-up

parts.words: The person planning for a constructive follow-up
parts.note: reads as someone hoping for a useful next step, but 'constructive' means building: the planner draws up designs that builders then follow

explanation.surface: Someone who is planning ahead for a productive next stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructive' means helpful in the surface; literally it is about construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's designer draws the plans that the builders carry out afterwards.

clue.text: A man taking a lot of interest in financial dealings

definitions.text: A man taking a lot of interest in financial dealings

parts.words: A man taking a lot of interest in financial dealings
parts.note: reads as someone keenly absorbed in money matters, but 'interest' is the charge on a loan, and this lender takes far too much of it

explanation.surface: A man who is fascinated by the world of finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a lot of interest' looks like enthusiasm; it means charging excessive interest on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging exorbitant rates on loans is the classic extortionate lender.

clue.text: Article carried by 20 across in flight

indicators.note: a piece carried by another sits inside it, so the article goes into the other light's letters

parts.note: the answer to 20 across, a word for move or a jail
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something is lifted along by a movement through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; a stair, in older use, can mean a whole flight of steps as well as a single step.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a set of steps between floors, which is also what a flight is.

clue.text: Withdraw soldiers over a wide area

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece over another is written above it, so the soldiers come first

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
a tract is an extensive stretch of land

explanation.surface: Pull the troops back across a broad stretch of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or pull in, so to withdraw a statement or a claw.

clue.text: Mention the source of information

definitions.meaning: a passing mention of something is an allusion to it
a book or document consulted for facts is a source cited in footnotes

explanation.surface: An instruction to credit where the information came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference is both an allusion made in passing and a work cited or consulted for facts.

clue.text: Bill represents the currently popular view

parts.note: something fashionable right now is 'in'
a voice is an expressed opinion or view, as in 'having a voice'

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation reflects what most people think at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a parliamentary bill to match 'popular view'; here it is a trader's bill. 'represents' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a trader's itemised demand for payment, a synonym of bill.

clue.text: Abandoned Conservative leader for a superior guy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here that of Conservative

parts.note: 'as' can mean 'for', as in 'used as/for a doorstop'
a toff is a well-dressed upper-class man

explanation.surface: A party leader has been dropped in favour of a posher candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cast off has been discarded or thrown aside, as abandoned things are.

clue.text: Men only backed the man and he's found work in a theatre

definitions.text: he's found work in a theatre

parts.note: a stag party or event is for men only

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the word for the man is read in reverse

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: An all-male group supported a fellow who then got a job at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support; it reverses HE to give EH.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand moves scenery and props behind the scenes during a show, a job backstage.

clue.text: Put off housing record, landed in a poultry-shed

indicators.note: one word housing another holds it inside, so the record and landed pieces go into put off

parts.note: to put off is to deter
EP is an extended-play record
a bird that has landed has alit or lit

explanation.surface: A bird, deterred by a recording, comes down inside a henhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' is the container signal. 'Put off' reads as a verb on the record; it is the outer piece. The definition describes where the answer is found, not what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep litter is a thick bed of straw or shavings spread over a hen-house floor, a traditional way of keeping chickens indoors.

clue.text: Having a credit-note, gives ground

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts; the run of letters across 'a credit' also spells the answer, a coincidence beside the charade
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Someone holding a credit note hands over a piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit-note' reads as one shop voucher; split it into CR and E. 'Having' and 'gives' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a measure of land, so a piece of ground can be called an acre.

clue.text: Short section of the matter set out

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from a whole, so the answer is a run of letters lying inside the next words

explanation.surface: A brief part of the subject is laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'matTER SEt'; 'out' finishes the surface and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse remark is brief and clipped, so it is short.

clue.text: The handling of someone who is patient?

definitions.text: The handling of someone who is patient?

parts.words: The handling of someone who is patient?
parts.note: reads as how to deal with a tolerant person, but 'patient' is a noun here: someone under a doctor's care, and how they are handled medically

explanation.surface: A question about how best to deal with a long-suffering person.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to someone sick, and more broadly the way a person is dealt with.

clue.text: Toiling for a living or getting money by corrupt means?

definitions.meaning: graft is British slang for hard work
graft is also bribery and dishonest gain, especially by officials

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone earns honestly or through bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers hard labour in British slang and political bribery or kickbacks in its other sense.

clue.text: Cheered a number with medical problem

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in disorder, so the letters of medical are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer's song was applauded despite a health complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medical problem' looks like an illness, but 'problem' alone is the anagram signal and 'medical' its fodder; 'number' is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer acclaimed by an audience has been loudly applauded and praised.

clue.text: Sped about at church to finish off

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of sped are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rushed round to a church to wrap things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal on 'Sped'; 'to' sits before the infinitive definition as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To despatch someone is to kill them quickly, which is to finish them off.

clue.text: Drink about ten? That's a bad sign!

indicators.note: about means around, so the drink goes around the number

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wanting a drink at ten in the morning is a worrying symptom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the number sits whole inside the drink, between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen, usually of something unwelcome, so an ill sign of things to come.

clue.text: Class of foreigners thrown by English

parts.note: a thing cast has been thrown

explanation.surface: A group of overseas students is thrown out by the English department.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase: the caste system is associated with India, seen from a British paper as foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: Castes are the hereditary social ranks of Hindu society, so a class among people from abroad.

clue.text: Concerned with getting behind because honest

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece getting behind another follows it, so the piece for concerned with comes last

parts.note: since can mean because
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone who backs a cause wholeheartedly because they are genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting behind' sounds like support; it is the order signal. 'because' looks like a link but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person means what they say, genuine and truthful.

clue.text: Move when it's cooler

definitions.meaning: to move, budge or start to be active
... and cooler are both slang terms for prison

explanation.surface: Advice to get going once the weather turns colder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' looks like temperature; it is slang for jail, as is the answer. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir means to move slightly, and as slang both it and 'cooler' mean a jail.

clue.text: No crate's in use, though receptacles are required

indicators.note: letters put to use are worked into a new form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the 's counts as a letter S here, giving crates

explanation.surface: No crate is available, but something to put things in is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in use' looks like a phrase; 'in' is part of the fodder and 'use' alone is the anagram signal on NO CRATES IN. 'though' and 'are required' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Containers are boxes, jars and other vessels that hold things, which is what receptacles are.

clue.text: Aches to be free to drive away

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order, so aches is rearranged

explanation.surface: Pains wanting to be released so they can leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase off is to drive someone away by pursuing them.

clue.text: Feel regret over accepting some decoration or other

indicators.note: one word accepting another takes it inside, so the decoration goes into the word for regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British decoration

explanation.surface: Someone sorry to have agreed to receive an award or other honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some decoration' gives CH; 'or other' then defines the answer as another kind of decoration, a dressmaking one. 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered frill of fabric used to trim a garment, a decoration in sewing rather than an honour.

clue.text: Common sorts left behind

indicators.note: one thing left behind another comes after it, so the left letter follows the sorts

parts.note: genera, plural of genus, are classes or sorts

explanation.surface: Ordinary people have been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left behind' reads as abandoned; split, 'left' gives L and 'behind' places it after GENERA.
explanation.definitionFit: General means shared by most or widespread, which is what common means.

clue.text: A trouble-maker one and all makes charges against

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
each means every one, one and all

explanation.surface: A troublemaker accuses everyone in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is formally to accuse an official of wrongdoing, which is to bring charges.

clue.text: Stagger the rag-and-bone man

definitions.meaning: to stagger is to walk unsteadily, to wobble
in British slang a ... is a scrap collector, a rag-and-bone man going from street to street with a cart buying old junk

explanation.surface: A scrap dealer walks unsteadily down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag-and-bone man is a British street trader who collects unwanted household junk; 'totting' is slang for that trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Totter means to walk unsteadily, and in London slang a scrap-collecting street trader is also called by that name.

clue.text: Stick a little notice in this spot

parts.note: an ad is a small advertisement, a short notice
here means in this spot

explanation.surface: Put up a small advertisement right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the pieces, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain fastened, so to stick.
